memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They joined five of the curtains together and did the same with the other five. Then they made loops of blue material along the edge of the end curtain in one set, and the same was done with the end curtain in the other set. They also made fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the other set, with the loops opposite each other." - Exod 36:10-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Fifty loops on one curtain. Fifty on the other. Positioned so that each one lines up exactly with its partner.

This is painstaking work with a simple purpose: separate pieces becoming one structure. And the joining had to be precise. A loop out of alignment meant a gap, and a gap in the desert meant wind, sand and rain getting in.

Scripture repeatedly describes God's people this way. We are being built together to become a dwelling in which God lives by His Spirit (Eph 2:22). Not standing side by side — joined.

That joining takes deliberate work. Fifty loops is not accidental; someone counted, measured and matched. Unity in a church or a family never happens by drifting. It happens through effort: making every effort to keep the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace (Eph 4:3).

Notice too that the loops had to face each other. Connection requires both sides to turn toward the other. One person reaching out while the other looks away joins nothing.

Is there a relationship where you have been waiting for the other person to turn first?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where in your life is a connection loose that needs repairing?
2. Are you making effort toward unity, or waiting for others?
3. What does it cost you to stay joined to difficult people?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, make me a person who joins rather than divides. Give me humility to turn toward those I have drifted from. Amen.
